mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC posted its first weekly improvement in four weeks (from -25.0 to -23.1), indicating the downward trend has lost momentum. This own-series inflection should persist as a mean-reverting recovery, pulling the 4-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC above the trailing 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -25.0 at t-1w to -23.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next four weekly RETAIL_REC means resume a decline and the 28-day forward mean falls below the trailing 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility stopped deteriorating in the latest week (-33.7 to -32.7), a leading indicator of renewed commuting and shopping trips. Once TRANSIT's week-on-week change turns positive after a multi-week decline, RETAIL_REC typically follows upward within two weeks as transit-dependent footfall returns to retail centers.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change turns positive after at least two prior weeks of decline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -33.7 at t-1w to -32.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT's positive week-on-week turn is not followed by a rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks (RETAIL_REC forward 2-week mean below trailing mean), the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous easing of WORKPLACES decline (-19.0 to -18.0) and a plateau/slight pullback in RESIDENTIAL (19.9 to 19.0) jointly signal that people are spending marginally less time at home and more time commuting, which interacts to amplify discretionary retail trips beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -19.0 to -18.0 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.9 to 19.0
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean despite both WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL falling concurrently, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As London moves into mid-October, declining daylight and cooler temperatures reduce outdoor park usage, visible in PARKS staying deeply negative (-11.0) versus earlier in the series. This seasonal shift redirects leisure activity indoors, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as substitution from parks to shopping/dining venues occurs.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained near -11 for the last two weeks versus -6.4 three weeks prior
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean fails to rise even as PARKS remains persistently depressed, the seasonal substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained elevated near +19 for three consecutive weeks, reflecting continued precautionary behavior consistent with lingering guidance to limit unnecessary trips. While this guidance persists, it suppresses discretionary retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed or declining further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 points for three or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 16.1 and 19.9 across all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean rises above its trailing mean while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 15, the suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC stabilized near -23 to -25 despite TRANSIT remaining deeply negative, suggesting behavioral decoupling where people increasingly use non-transit modes (walking, cycling, private cars) to reach retail destinations. This adaptive behavior should sustain a modest near-term uptick in RETAIL_REC independent of transit trends over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved while TRANSIT remained near -33 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines in the next week while TRANSIT also stays flat or worsens, the decoupling hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (such as the -6.4 to -20.6 plunge two weeks ago) reflects a sudden weather-driven shift away from outdoor activity. When such a sharp PARKS decline occurs, substitution to indoor retail and recreation venues should raise RETAIL_REC within the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -6.4 at t-3w to -20.6 at t-2w, a 14.2 point drop
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not rise following a PARKS drop exceeding 10 points, the threshold substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed flat near +1 percent throughout the snapshot, indicating essential-shopping demand is saturated and stable. When this stability coincides with a recovering TRANSIT series, any additional mobility gains are likely discretionary rather than essential, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks beyond what TRANSIT alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow -1.6 to +1.6 band across all four weeks while TRANSIT improved slightly in the last week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean does not exceed its trailing mean despite stable GROCERY_PHARM and improving TRANSIT, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
